MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 14, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:00 p.m., on December 14, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on December 9, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell (arrived 5:02pm)
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Member Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation (Paragraph 1 of Subdivision (d) )
  of Government Code Section 54956.9: Jann Kronik-Gath vs. City Council

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project v.
  The City of Mission Viejo.`

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with five City Council Members present.
City Council Minutes  1  December 14, 2021
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were two closed session items on litigation and
that there was no reportable actions and the City Council was updated.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1. State of the City

  Received the State of the City.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Luke Alvarado, Newport Beach: Introduced that he was the President of LandForms Landscape
Construction. He stated that he is protesting the Coronado Park Play Area Rehabilitation (CIP 328)
contract award to Micon Construction. He outlined his reasons.

Ben Green, Huntington Beach: Introduced that he is Vice President of LandForms and agreed with
Speaker Luke Alvarado on protesting the award of contract to Micon Construction.

Connie Lanzisera, M.V.: Explained that she spoke at a Council Meeting about seven months ago
regarding her concerns over the sober living home in her neighborhood. She updated the City
Council on the problems in her neighborhood with this home and pleaded with the City to send
correspondence to the State to fight against these homes in Mission Viejo.

Lisa Foto, M.V.: Expressed her frustration with the Sober Living Homes throughout Orange
County and outlined her concerns with the medical treatment in the home in her neighborhood.

Augie Cortez, M.V.: Spoke out against the Garden Plaza potential project of a high-rise apartment
complex.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Suggested to the City Council to adopt a requirement that any new
housing development in the City that 15% of the housing be affordable.

Sean Doran, M.V.: Stated that the information on the Garden Plaza was not misinformation and
that it was pulled from the City’s website. Indicated that the flyer did not state that this item was
on the agenda this evening. It encouraged residents to speak against the proposal of such a
project.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Voiced concerns on the extended terms of the City Council Member in both
2018 and 2020. He does not feel he has received an answer to the concerns he has with regards to
their terms.

City Council Minutes  2  December 14, 2021
 Vikki Rixford, M.V.: Spoke out against the Garden Plaza potential project and reminded the
Council that Mission Viejo is a planned community and that there is no place for high rise
apartment complexes.

Rafael Reyes, M.V.: Expressed his concerns in his neighborhood of a substance abuse center that
will be opening and asked for the Council’s assistance in this matter.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 16 and 23 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
remainder of the Consent Calendar as outlined below. On roll call, said motion carried by the
following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT: None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of November 9, 2021, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated October 29, 2021 in the Amount of $590,374.40

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated November 5, 2021 in the Amount of $4,046,218.03

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated November 12, 2021 in the Amount of $1,081,802.89

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated November 19, 2021 in the Amount of $988,953.43

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated November 26, 2021 in the Amount of $415,671.55

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  December 14, 2021
 7.  Fiscal Year 2020/21 Mission Viejo Housing Authority Annual Report

  Received and filed the report.

8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2021

  Received and filed the report.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for October 2021

  Received and filed the report.

10. Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for October 2021

  Received and filed the report.

11. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October
  2021

  Received and filed the report.

12. Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Fiscal
  Year Ended June 30, 2021 and Related Reports

  Received and filed the report.

13. Annual Measure M2 Expenditure Report for Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2021

  Approved Resolution 21-44 Adopting the Measure M2 Expenditure Report for the City of
  Mission Viejo.

14. Federal Transportation Improvement Program

  Adopt Resolution 21-45 Certifying that the City of Mission Viejo has the Resources to Fund
  the Projects in the FY's 2022/23 - 2027/28 Transportation Improvement Program and
  Affirming its Commitment to Implement all Projects in the Program.

15. Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park Field Lighting (CIP 331)

  Awarded a contract for Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park Field Lighting design services and
  preparation of construction drawings and documents to RJM Design Group (A21-56) in an
  amount not to exceed $62,750.00.

City Council Minutes  4  December 14, 2021
 17. Landscape and Irrigation Supplies

  Approved Fifth Amendment with SiteOne Landscape Supply to authorize change order to
  the existing Purchase Order in an amount not to exceed $100,000.00 for the purchase of
  smart irrigation controllers.

18. Public Works Inspection Services

  Approved a Purchase Order with Onward Engineering for as-needed Public Works
  Inspection Services for a fee not to exceed $49,680.00.

19. Plumbing Related Services at City Facilities

  Approved First Amendment with Santa Margarita Plumbing and Air, Inc. for plumbing
  related services at city facilities for the period of July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022.

20. Oso Creek Golf Course Prefabricated Restroom Building

  Awarded contract to Sun Pac Storage Containers, Inc. (A21-58) for the purchase and
  delivery of the prefabricated restroom building at Oso Creek Golf Course in an amount not
  to exceed $51,677.74.

21. Replacement of Exterior Doors and Installation of New Sliding Interior Door- Oso
  Creek Golf Course Clubhouse - Notice of Completion

  1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days, respectively, after the
  date of the Notice of Completion recordation and contingent upon the absence of claims or
  liens being filed with the City; and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of
  $4,676.98, thirty-five (35) days after the date of the Notice of Completion recordation.

22. Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning Related Services at City Hall and Library

  Approved First Amendment with South Coast Mechanical for HVAC related services and
  repairs at City Hall and the Library for the period of July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022 in an
  amount not to exceed $61,000.00.

24. Review and Approval of Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 22-23 A-B
  Annual Fiscal Period of July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2023

  (1) Adopted Successor Agency Resolution 21-02 Approving the Recognized Obligation
  Payment Schedule 22-23 A-B for the Annual Fiscal Period of July 1, 2022 to June 30, 2023,
  Subject to Submittal to and Review by the Orange Countywide Oversight Board and by the
  Department of Finance Under the Division 24, Part 1.85 of the California Health and Safety

City Council Minutes  5  December 14, 2021
   Code, and Authorizing the Posting and Transmittal Thereof; and (2) further, the Director of
  Administrative Services, in consultation with legal counsel, shall be authorized to request
  and complete meet and confer session(s), if any, with the Department of Finance and
  authorized to make augmentations, modifications, additions or revisions as may be
  necessary or directed by the Department of Finance.

25. Montanoso Recreation Center Rehabilitation - (CIP 314)

  Approved the Plans and Specifications and authorize staff to advertise for bids for (CIP 314)
  - Montanoso Recreation Center Rehabilitation.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

16.  Coronado Park Play Area Rehabilitation (CIP 328)

  Director of Public Services Jerry Hill presented the staff report.

  Council Member Sachs asked that the Council table this item until we look at the complaints
  that were spoken about this project under public comments.

  Director Jerry Hill addressed the protest complaint by LandForms and explained to the
  Council that Micon was the valid low bidder.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to (1) award contract
  to Micon Construction, Inc.(A21-57) for the Coronado Park Play Area Rehabilitation - CIP
  328, in an amount not to exceed $625,854.00; and (2) approve issuance of Purchase Order for
  the purchase of shade covers for Coronado Park Play Area Rehabilitation - CIP 328 to Great
  Western Recreation in the amount of $87,379.06.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, and Kelley
  NOES:  Raths and Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

23. La Paz Bridge Rehabilitation and Road Widening Improvements (CIP 01756)

  Council Member Sachs stated he was excited to see this project moving forward and
  congratulated staff in their continual efforts to move this project through.

  Directory of Public Works gave the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) award the
  construction contract for the subject project to Security Paving Company (A21-59) in the
  amount of $13,593,657; and (2) adopt Resolution 21-46 Amending the Fiscal Year 2021-2022
  Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Project (CIP 01756).

City Council Minutes  6  December 14, 2021
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

26. Presentation of Map A, a Mission Viejo City Council Districting Proposal

  Center for Demographic Research Consultant Deborah Diep presented the report.

  Mayor Kelley opened the Public Hearing at 8:07 p.m.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Pointed out discrepancies of Map Z from 2018 and gerrymandering.
  Questioned the score of Map A that is presented tonight and asked that Mayor Kelley
  resident be identified on any map under consideration.

  Mayor Kelley closed the Public Hearing at 8:10 p.m.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1)
  receive presentation by the Center for Demographic Research regarding the 2020 Census data
  and related district mapping process and criteria; (2) discussed the California Elections Code
  and State and Federal Constitutional requirements for district formation; (3) received City
  Council and public comments on Map A; and (4) received Map A and discuss the process by
  which the public and City Council Members can submit alternative district Map
  configurations that satisfy legal requirements.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

27. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum.

28. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Kelley.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

29. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234
City Council Minutes  7  December 14, 2021
   By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell congratulated Mayor Kelley and Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum on the great
job they did this past year and is looking forward to the new year.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths stated that he represented the City at the Gypsum Canyon Veteran’s
Cemetery Groundbreaking event. Congratulated Mayor Kelley and Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum on
a great year. He wished everyone a happy holiday.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs reiterated that one thing during comments that the City Attorney mentioned
was very important to residents to understand regarding housing in the City. Stressed that
Sacramento has stripped local control when it comes to housing. He thanked the Mayor answering
all the emails that have poured in from residents. Wished everyone a Merry Christmas and Happy
New Year.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

30. City of Mission Viejo Support for the Local Government Land Use Initiative

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum presented her report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to adopt Resolution
  21-47 Supporting the Brand-Huang-Mendoza Tripartisan Land Use Initiative to Amend
  Article XI of the Constitution of the State of California and Enable Local Governments to
  Retain Local Land Use Control and Override State Control and State Mandates.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum stated she is pleased with the initial districting map that was presented
this evening. Thanked staff for being supportive in the effort with the residents who spoke about
the Garden Plaza. Stated that the Council has to wait until plans are submitted and have to be
cautious about our position because we have to give every resident a fair opportunity to present
their concerns. Complimented Mayor Kelly and their working relationship. Lastly, she quoted to

City Council Minutes  8  December 14, 2021
 Mayor Kelley from Proverbs, “Wisdom calls out in the street, she makes her voice heard in the
public squares, she cries out above the commotion, she speaks at the entrance of the city gates.”

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley announced that has been a month since the last meeting and highlighted a few events
that she attended. Encouraged residents to watch the Veteran’s Day Ceremony if they were unable
to attend. She also attended along with Council Member Raths the Veteran’s Day observance at
the Orange County Cemetery District located in Lake Forest. Stated that she and Mayor Pro Tem
Bucknum attended the Hanukah celebration at Pavion Park to see the menorah being lit. She also
attended a ribbon cutting ceremony at Domenico’s restaurant on the lake. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
and herself attended the Animal Shelter holiday celebration and they got to see the Barn in person.
She thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for Santa’s Arrival. Announced the ongoing
toy drive for the marine families and thanked residents that contributed. Lastly, she thanked her
colleagues and staff for the past year.

CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

31. Selection of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for 2022

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to appoint Wendy
  Bucknum to serve as Mayor in 2022.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to appoint Ed
  Sachs to serve as Mayor Pro Tem in 2022.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:54 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting tin memory of Carl Glassford to Tuesday, January 11, 2022,
at 5:00 p.m.

City Council Minutes  9  December 14, 2021
 ______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 11, 2022

City Council Minutes  10  December 14, 2021
